verses.english: Linked Discourses 44.11
1. The Undeclared Points
With Sabhiya Kaccāna

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā sabhiyo kaccāno ñātike viharati giñjakāvasathe.
verses.english: At one time Venerable Sabhiya Kaccāna was staying at Ñātika in the brick house.

verses.pali: Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako yenāyasmā sabhiyo kaccāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sabhiyena kaccānena saddhiṁ sammodi.
verses.english: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta went up to him, and exchanged greetings with him.

verses.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako āyasmantaṁ sabhiyaṁ kaccānaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side, and said to Sabhiya Kaccāna:

verses.pali: “kiṁ nu kho bho, kaccāna, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
verses.english: “Worthy Kaccāna, does a realized one still exist after death?”
“Vaccha, this has not been declared by the Buddha.”

verses.pali: “Kiṁ pana, bho kaccāna, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
verses.english: “Well then, does a realized one no longer exist after death?”
“This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

verses.pali: “Kiṁ nu kho, bho kaccāna, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
verses.english: “Well then, does a realized one both exist and not exist after death?”
“This has not been declared by the Buddha.”

verses.pali: ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Kiṁ pana, bho kaccāna, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā”ti?
verses.english: “Well then, does a realized one neither exist nor not exist after death?”
“This too has not been declared by the Buddha.”

verses.pali: ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho kaccāna, hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
verses.english: “Worthy Kaccāna, when asked these questions, you say that this has not been declared by the Buddha.

verses.pali: ‘Kiṁ pana, bho kaccāna, na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ nu kho, bho kaccāna, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi.
‘Kiṁ pana, bho kaccāna, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti vadesi.
Ko nu kho, bho kaccāna, hetu, ko paccayo, yenetaṁ abyākataṁ samaṇena gotamenā”ti?
verses.english: What’s the cause, what’s the reason why this has not been declared by the Buddha?”

verses.pali: “Yo ca, vaccha, hetu, yo ca paccayo paññāpanāya rūpīti vā arūpīti vā saññīti vā asaññīti vā nevasaññīnāsaññīti vā, so ca hetu, so ca paccayo sabbena sabbaṁ sabbathā sabbaṁ aparisesaṁ nirujjheyya.
verses.english: “In order to describe him as ‘formed’ or ‘formless’ or ‘percipient’ or ‘non-percipient’ or ‘neither percipient nor non-percipient’, there must be some cause or reason for doing so. But if that cause and reason were to totally and utterly cease without remainder,

verses.pali: Kena naṁ paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya rūpīti vā arūpīti vā saññīti vā asaññīti vā nevasaññīnāsaññīti vā”ti.
verses.english: how could you describe him in any such terms?”
“Worthy Kaccāna, how long has it been since you went forth?”
“Not long, reverend: three years.”

verses.pali: “Yassapassa, āvuso, etamettakena ettakameva tampassa bahu, ko pana vādo evaṁ abhikkante”ti.
verses.english: “One who has learned this much in this time, reverend, has learned a lot, who can say what lies ahead!”
The Linked Discourses on undeclared questions are complete.
The Book of the Six Sense Fields is finished.
